system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.
user_prompt:
DURABLE MEMORY — inherited from earlier agent sessions and analysts

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    Avoid broad 40% discounts: acquisition and revenue gains trade off against 12% lower retention. Measured in the standard SMB segment.

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

answer.rationale: The two acute, measurable deficits are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so fixing it can move both. Inherited memory supports this twice over: memory_86 (shorter onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value across self-serve) and memory_31 (fewer required signup fields produced a durable SMB activation lift). Because those two records are the entire basis for the action and are 24-52 days old, they are exactly what I spend the verification budget on — I want the original records to confirm segment (SMB self-serve), effect size, and whether the lift was measured as durable rather than a transient novelty bump. I did not verify memory_73; I am not proposing discounting, so its value is as a guardrail, not a decision input. The competitor's entry pricing creates real pressure to answer with promotional_pricing, but memory_73 explicitly prices that trade: acquisition/revenue gains against 12% lower retention, which is the wrong trade against a sustainable long-term qualified revenue objective — and matching a price war on a competitor's terms compounds it. referral_incentive (memory_57) is sound but works through established customers and does not touch the failing funnel step. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is credible but addresses a segment that is not the one bleeding. activation_messaging (memory_91) is the closest alternative and would be my fallback if verification undercuts the onboarding records; I favor onboarding because it is the upstream cause and the fix is structural rather than a nudge. Downstream value risk is flagged: cutting required fields can shift measured gains into lower-quality signups, so the experiment must read qualified-revenue and retention cohorts, not just completion and first-week activation. Uncertainty preserved: these memories are consolidated summaries, the prior lifts were measured before the current competitive shift, and the current declines may share a cause (competitor siphoning price-sensitive accounts) that onboarding changes cannot address — so I run this as an instrumented standard experiment with a retention/quality readout rather than a broad rollout, and treat a null result as informative about that alternative cause.
